description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been holding talks in the Gulf. 
He wants to reassure America's allies in the region that Washington will prioritise their security in the wake of the Iran agreement. 
While meeting GCC officials in Manama, Rubio said the US wants a permanent deal with Tehran, but not at any price. 
He also insisted Iran should not charge for ships to cross the Strait of Hormuz and should never possess a nuclear weapon. 
All of this comes with the background of the unprecedented attacks that were launched against Gulf states by Iran. 
The GCC is now pushing for a bigger say in what happens in its own backyard. This includes security and the Strait of Hormuz. 
But can Washington ease Gulf concerns and ensure their voices will be heard? 


Presenter: James Bays

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
What led to the war?

On February 28, 2026, the US and Israel launched massive strikes on Iran, claiming an imminent nuclear threat.

This film traces how the world reached this point after more than three decades of shadow war over “the bomb”.

Israel has tried to block Tehran’s nuclear drive with sabotage, assassinations and cyberwar – from the Stuxnet virus wrecking Natanz centrifuges to the AI-assisted killing of nuclear programme “father” Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, and a commando raid stealing 1.5 tonnes of secret nuclear archive files.

Iran insists uranium enrichment is its sovereign right and key to national identity and regional power.

As Israel pounded Iran’s nuclear facilities in June 2025 and systematically weakened its allies in Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen, nuclear talks continued in Geneva. Iran was edging towards diluting weapons-grade uranium – but Israel wasn’t prepared to wait, and pulled Washington into open war whose global consequences are only now beginning to unfol
title: How Israel's shadow war on Iran ended in open conflict | Featured Documentary

The government has responded by blending petrol with ethanol — a biofuel derived from maize, rice and sugarcane — which officials say has saved at least 16 billion dollars in foreign exchange over the past decade. India is also diversifying its oil suppliers, turning to Russia, West Africa and the Americas to reduce its reliance on the Middle East.

Two powerful earthquakes have struck Venezuela west of the capital Caracas on a public holiday, catching the country off guard. The first, a magnitude 7.2 quake at a depth of 22 kilometres, was followed just 39 seconds later by a stronger 7.5 magnitude tremor at 10 kilometres. Buildings were levelled or left badly damaged, while panic broke out at the country’s main international airport. Witnesses described scenes of chaos, with one saying it was “like a horror movie” as residents climbed over rubble to escape.
Interim President Delcy Rodríguez says at least 32 people have been killed and more than 700 injured, ordering the evacuation of buildings with severe structural damage. Hundreds of emergency responders are continuing search and rescue operations, while authorities have declared a nationwide emergency. US officials have also pledged support and humanitarian assistance, according to reports.

description:
Rising fuel prices linked to disruption caused by the Iran war are accelerating China's shift towards electric vehicles. In Beijing, new EV owner Du Pan says soaring petrol costs pushed him to abandon his fuel-powered car, joining a growing number of Chinese drivers making the switch. China is already the world's largest electric vehicle market, with more than half of all new car sales now battery-powered. The trend comes as China's crude oil imports have fallen sharply, with analysts suggesting demand could decline permanently as EV adoption increases. Higher oil prices are also driving efforts to electrify heavy vehicles, with Beijing targeting 40 percent of new truck sales to be electric by 2030. Analysts say a sustained reduction in Chinese oil demand could have significant implications for global energy markets, given China's status as the world's largest crude importer.

Al Jazeera's Katrina Yu reports from Beijing, China.
